title: Grain direction, edging and allowances
intro: A finished part dimension may differ from its core cutting dimension. Specify grain, edge treatment and measurement stage, then calculate allowances from the defined construction.
goals: Specify grain direction for each part
Calculate core size from defined edges

sections.title: Specify grain direction for each part
sections.text: Place a grain arrow on the identified face. For adjacent fronts, state orientation and sequence when a continuous appearance is required. Rotating a rectangle in a cutting layout may save material but change grain. Do not assume the first scheduled dimension defines grain direction; record it separately.
sections.caption: A grain arrow is independent of dimension order.

sections.title: Calculate core size from defined edges
sections.text: In this declared exercise, finished width is 400 mm and opposite edges each receive an assumed 1 mm band, with no other additions in that direction. Core width is 400 − 1 − 1 = 398 mm; one banded edge would give 399 mm. Label stage, edges and system. This geometric assumption is not a universal product recipe.
sections.caption: Exercise only: 400 finished = 1 edge + 398 core + 1 edge.

sections.title: Document allowance and operation
sections.text: Distinguish rough preparation stock from edge deductions and assembly clearances. Saw kerf affects sheet layout, not an automatic addition to each finished part. Record finished, core and rough-stage dimensions with reasons. A 402 mm schedule entry against a 400 mm drawing requires clarification of stage or revision, rather than an unexplained correction.
sections.caption: Every dimensional difference needs a stage and reason.

example.title: Worked case and decision
example.text: Both exercise fronts finish at 400 mm width. P01 has two 1 mm opposite bands, giving a 398 mm core; P02 has one 1 mm band, giving 399 mm. Mark E1/E2, grain and measurement stage. A bare 400 mm entry does not establish the required cut size.
example.decision: Decision: schedule 398 and 399 mm as core sizes under the documented exercise assumptions.

quiz.question: For a 400 mm finished width with two 1 mm bands, what is the exercise core width?

assignment.prompt: Prepare P01/P02 rows, a face sketch with grain and edge IDs, and a table of finished/core dimensions with reasons.

faq.question: Should kerf be added to every finished part?
faq.answer: No. Account for it in the sheet layout separately from finished part dimensions.
